Johansson, D., Sjöblom, J. and Berntsson, T. (2012). Heat supply alternatives for CO2 capture in the process industry. International Journal of Greenhouse Gas Control 8, 217-232. doi:10.1016/j.ijggc.2012.02.007

Locators are printed journal pages (217-232 = PDF pages 1-16). Case study: MEA post-combustion capture (85%) on the Borealis steam cracker furnace flue gas (Stenungsund, Sweden; 566 kt CO2/y; 8% CO2), five heat-supply options (NGCC, natural gas boiler, biomass boiler, each with a back-pressure turbine; current excess heat with heat pump; energy-optimised excess heat) at two specific reboiler duties (2800, 4700 kJ/kg CO2). Loaded: Table 6 (2030) per option x duty: capture-unit capacity, steam duty, electricity per t (MW x 8000 h / kt), capex per t-per-yr and non-energy OPEX per t captured; heat-supply unit capacity, fuel per GJ steam, heat-to-power ratio and capex per kW steam; heat-pump COP and temperatures (Tables 1-2); Table 7 (existing boilers at full load) capture-unit rows and existing-boiler gas use; headline 37-70 EUR/t avoided for excess-heat options. TRAPS: (1) every investment in Tables 6-7 is ANNUALISED (kEUR/y, annuity 0.089); capex here is derived by dividing by 0.089 (formula shows it); (2) Table 7 OPEX for NGCC(steam) 4700 printed 66,068 kEUR/y is a misprint (specific OPEX implies ~6,068): not loaded; (3) Table 7 prints CO2 from cracker plant as 566,186 kt/y (unit should be t/y); (4) capture-plant scope includes the flue-gas blower and CO2 compression to ~75 bar; (5) avoidance costs by scenario and year exist only in Figs. 11-15 (not transcribed). Price year 2010 EUR throughout. UKERC 2013 rows CH-SC28 to CH-SC37 cite this paper: they use 3750 kJ/kg (mean of the paper's 2800 and 4700 cases) and their even-row capex equals the paper's ANNUALISED total investment (mean of the two duties) x 1.03e-3 per t of cracker product, i.e. UKERC appears to have treated an annualised cost as a capital cost; odd rows add a constant 435.3 GBP/t-yr cracker capex.
